amendments.rule: **The *that* of a presentative `הָיָה` belongs to that verb, and is not `added`.** The ASV renders `וַיְהִי` and `וְהָיָה` with a frame — *And it came to pass … that*, *And it shall come to pass … that* — and the frame's complementizer is part of what the verb is rendered by, exactly as rule 21's dummy subject is. It joins the `הָיָה` unit, headed as that unit already heads. The unit may be discontinuous under rule 25 where a temporal phrase stands inside the frame: `וְהָיָה אַחֲרֵי כֵן` → *And it shall come to pass afterward, that* gives `הָיָה` both *it shall come to pass* and *that*, while `אַחֲרֵי כֵן` keeps *afterward*. **Where the apodosis opens with its own waw, that waw carries the *that* instead** and the verb keeps only *it came to pass*; and where the ASV writes no *that* at all there is nothing to place. Read which of the three the verse is rather than reaching for the verb every time. **And where what stands inside the frame is not a phrase but a temporal clause the ASV writes with a relative or complementizer of its own, the frame's *that* is the one standing at the head of the apodosis, never the first one written.** Read the Hebrew for where the apodosis begins and count the ASV's *that*s against the clauses that license them, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s: a *that* introducing the temporal clause answers to whatever morpheme rules 52 and 19 put it on, and only the *that* the ASV writes before the apodosis is the frame's. `וְהָיָה בְּיוֹם הַנְחִילוֹ אֶת־בָּנָיו ... לֹא יוּכַל לְבַכֵּר` → *then it shall be in the day* ***that*** *he causeth his sons to inherit that which he hath,* ***that*** *he may not make the son of the beloved the first born* gives the second *that* to `הָיָה`, discontinuous across the whole temporal clause under rule 25, and the first to the infinitive construct, exactly as rule 52 leaves *when they shall make* to the infinitive of `בְּיוֹם הֵעָשׂוֹתוֹ` where the `בְּ` and the construct noun each already hold an English word of their own. Do not mark the apodosis *that* `added` under rule 55 on the ground that no conjunction stands in its clause: the frame licenses it, and a frame whose complementizer has been spent on the temporal clause will always leave one over.
amendments.why: Rule 45 allowed a temporal phrase inside the frame but said nothing about a temporal clause carrying a complementizer of its own, which is what DEU.21.16 writes. The verse pass read the first 'that' as the frame's, which forced the apodosis 'that' into an added unit and left the temporal clause's relative unassigned to the morpheme rule 52 already gives it. The amendment states the count that decides it and cites rule 52's existing בְּיוֹם example, which the corpus already carries; nothing in the corpus rows contradicts it, and the וְהָיָה-plus-temporal-clause shape recurs throughout the law codes and the prophets, so the next pass to meet it would make the same error against the rule as it stood.

conventions: וְהָיָה frame: the frame's complementizer is the 'that' the ASV writes at the head of the APODOSIS, not the first 'that' in the verse. DEU.21.3 writes it contiguously ('it shall be that the city ... shall take'); DEU.21.16 writes it after a full temporal clause whose own 'that' belongs to the infinitive construct of בְּיוֹם הַנְחִילוֹ under rule 52, so the frame's 'that' is the one before 'he may not make'; DEU.21.14 writes none and there is nothing to place. Count the ASV's 'that's against the clauses that license them before assigning any of them, and do not mark the apodosis one added.

אֵינֶנּוּ שֹׁמֵעַ בְּקוֹל (DEU.21.18, DEU.21.20): אַיִן keeps the negation and heads on it (rule 50); the participle keeps 'will ... obey', the auxiliary staying with the predicate because the ASV writes the negation and the auxiliary as two words (rule 35); the בְּ is unrepresented, its object promoted to a bare direct object of 'obey' (rule 40); and the suffix takes whichever pronoun the ASV's recasting writes for it — the relative 'that' where the clause is recast as a relative modifying בֵּן (rule 18), the referential 'he' where the clause stands on its own. The two verses differ only in what the ASV wrote, and a present pronominal morpheme takes that word before any supplied-relative analysis (rule 11).

report: One real split: the presentative frame of וְהָיָה is analysed two ways. DEU.21.3 gives הָיָה a contiguous 'it shall be that'; DEU.21.16 gave it 'it shall be' plus the FIRST 'that' in the verse — which is the relative of the temporal clause 'in the day that he causeth' — and then had to mark the apodosis 'that' (t019) added. Rule 45 puts the frame's complementizer at the head of the apodosis, discontinuous under rule 25, and rule 52's בְּיוֹם הֵעָשׂוֹתוֹ leaves the temporal clause's own relative to the infinitive.

DEU.21.16 patched accordingly: הָיָה now holds t002 t003 t004 t019 headed on 'be', הַנְחִיל holds t008 t010 t013 t014 headed on 'inherit', and the added unit is gone. DEU.21.3 and DEU.21.14 (which writes no 'that' at all) were already right and are untouched. All 29 source and 42 target ids remain partitioned exactly once; the chapter now carries 5 added units, not 6.

Checked and rejected as splits, each licensed by the source or by the English the ASV actually wrote: אֵינֶנּוּ שֹׁמֵעַ at 21.18 ('that') against 21.20 ('he'), where the ASV recasts one clause as a relative and rule 18 gives the suffix the relative that realizes it; הָיָה rendered 'have committed' at 21.22 heading on 'have' where 21.7, 21.8, 21.14 and 21.15 head their perfects on the participle, because there the participle realizes the Hebrew verb's own lexeme and here it does not; אֶל־תּוֹךְ split at 21.12 against עַל־פְּנֵי fused at 21.16 (rule 30's one-rendering condition); the added connectives at 21.1 and 21.3, where no waw stands, against the 'and if' and 'and though' pairs at 21.15 and 21.18, where one does; the 'that city' determiner going to הִוא with both articles unrepresented at 21.3, 21.4, 21.6 and 21.7, against 'the same day' at 21.23 where the ASV writes two determiners and rule 41's count gives each morpheme one.

BSB: no genuine error among the 31 disagreements. The R×15 and Td×9 blocks are the documented convention difference — prepositions and articles the ASV's recasting leaves with no English (rules 29, 40). The named singletons are resumptive suffixes inside relative clauses (21.4 בּוֹ, 21.10 שִׁבְיוֹ), waws the ASV leaves unrendered (21.18, 21.21), object markers (21.19, 21.22) and the bare temporal accusative 'the same day' (21.23). Each is what rules 16, 22, 14 and 40 require; nothing here was changed to move the aggregate.

Two conventions recorded (הָיָה-frame complementizer placement; the אֵינֶנּוּ שֹׁמֵעַ clause across 21.18 and 21.20). One amendment returned, to rule 45, which is where this chapter's error lives: the rule already allows a temporal phrase inside the frame but says nothing about a temporal CLAUSE that carries a 'that' of its own, which is what made the first 'that' look like the frame's.
